title: Book 9 — Calliope, Chapter 63
paragraphs: In the place where Mardonius himself was — riding on a white horse and having around him the thousand best Persians picked from the rest — there they pressed upon their opponents most of all. As long as Mardonius was alive, they held out and in defending themselves cut down many of the Lacedaemonians; but when Mardonius was killed and the men ranged around his person (the strongest portion of the whole army) had fallen, then the others also turned and gave way before the Lacedaemonians. Their manner of dress, without defensive armor, was a very great cause of destruction to them, since in truth they were fighting light-armed against hoplites.
